text: We evaluated repeated self-distillation of the student's own labels, run for 2 distill rounds, with pythia-410m as the weak supervisor and mistral-7b as the strong student, across 4 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.6 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.76; the transfer accuracy after distillation was 0.73 with a standard error of 0.02. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.79 with a standard error of 0.14, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.55. Because the standard error on PGR is large relative to the separation from the baseline, the observed gap falls within two standard errors, so this run does not establish an improvement over the baseline; the direction is suggestive but the four-seed sample is too small to support a confident claim. Replication with more seeds, and ideally additional distillation rounds, would be needed to determine whether the apparent PGR advantage is real.
